title: Conversation-level latency analyzer for streaming vs synchronous routes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a Grafana/Console board and investigation flow that attributes tail latency at the conversation level, comparing streaming and synchronous IO modes across model/route. This ticket implements: 1) a conversation decomposition panel that splits end-to-end time into client network, proxy, routing, model-serving (kernel/batching/KV cache), and post-processing; 2) a streaming-tail overlay that surfaces per-token tail behavior (p50/p95/p99) and highlights requests with repeated small streaming tokens vs large chunked sync responses; 3) correlation between trace span annotations (trace hooks) and metrics/log evidence to pinpoint whether latency is due to batching, kernel stalls, KV cache cold misses, or network reassembly.

Scope: Instrumentation (trace hook additions + span tags), metrics pipelines (histogram labels by model, route, io_mode, cache_state), dashboard panels and alert query templates, and a short runbook for SRE/SEs. Excludes work to change runtime kernel behavior or autoscaling policies — this is observability-only.

Data sources: distributed traces (trace_id, spans with io_mode tag), request_duration histograms in Prometheus, KV cache metrics (hit/miss counters), batch sizing histograms, and structured request logs (request_id, route, model, stream_session_id).

Deliverables: 1) new "Conversation Decomposition" dashboard in Console with p50/p95/p99 breakdown and streaming tail visual; 2) a set of PromQL/SQL query templates for incident runbooks; 3) PRs for tracing hook changes (runtime + ingress proxy) and metrics pipeline transformations to attach io_mode and cache_state labels; 4) acceptance tests validating decomposition sums to <= observed end-to-end +/-5% for synthetic traces.

Success criteria: Dashboard surfaces root cause in >80% of synthetic injected anomalies (batching glitch, cache cold start, kernel stall), investigation median time-to-assign root cause <= 12 minutes during tabletop tests.
acceptance_criteria: Conversation decomposition panel shows components that sum to end-to-end within +/-5% on synthetic traces
Panels expose p50/p95/p99 for both streaming and synchronous IO modes per model and per route
Streaming-tail overlay highlights top 5 streaming sessions by token-level p99 and links to trace IDs
Tracing hooks emit io_mode and cache_state tags for every model-serving entry span (runtime PRs merged)
Metrics pipeline emits request_duration histogram with labels: model, route, io_mode, cache_state
Runbook contains at least three root-cause playbooks (batching, kernel stall, cache cold miss) with queries and next steps
comments: 2025-02-11 — Aisha Patel: Scoping call with SRE and Runtime teams. Agreed to add io_mode and cache_state span tags. Runtime team will add a lightweight span attribute to avoid perf penalty. Action: Marco to open runtime PR for trace tags.

2025-02-14 — Marco Chen: Drafted runtime change set (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4217). Adds 'io_mode' on entering model handler and emits 'cache_state' based on KV hit/miss. Benchmarked 1.6% P50 median overhead on local perf harness (acceptable).

2025-02-17 — Design review (Lina Morales): Feedback to ensure dashboard color legend maps same across panels; prefer stacked waterfall for decomposition. Lina asked for a compact table view for quick incident triage — added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-19 — SRE (Daniel Kim): Alert templates proposed for streaming-tail spike (increase in token-level p99 over baseline). Will test in staging with chaos injections. Linked inject job: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/streams-latency-inject

2025-02-22 — Marco Chen: Metrics pipeline transform merged (github.com/redwood/observability/pull/89). Added route/model/io_mode/cache_state labels to request_duration histogram. Also added batch_size histogram labels. Updated Grafana data source mapping.

2025-02-24 — QA (Priya Rao): Ran synthetic scenarios: 1) cache cold start, 2) oversized batching, 3) kernel stall. Conversation decomposition correctly flagged cache_state=mismatch in 9/10 cache cold tests; batching anomaly detected in 8/10. Identified one false negative where short streaming sessions were misattributed to network — traced to missing stream_session_id in some ingress logs. Assigned follow-up: ENG-67288 (ingress stream_session_id propagation).

2025-02-26 — Marco Chen: Dashboard prototype available: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/conv-decomp/conv-decomposition-board — shared with PM and SRE for early feedback. Added link in Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Conversation+Decomposition+Dashboard
2025-02-27 — Aisha Patel: Removed 'autoscale recommendations' from scope to keep this ticket focused. Follow-ups will be created for mitigation automations after dashboard stabilizes.
queries_examples: PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route, io_mode, cache_state))
PromQL: sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (model, route) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m])) by (model, route)  # cache miss rate
SQL (clickhouse): select route, io_mode, quantileExact(0.99)(duration_ms) from request_spans where timestamp >= now()-interval 1 hour group by route, io_mode
PromQL: topk(5, increase(stream_token_tail_latency_bucket{le="1000"}[15m])) by (stream_session_id)  # candidates for streaming-tail investigation
